headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: nullclaw’s broad egress and workspace access can expose content-writing outputs to a CRM agent that reads/writes files and uses MCP.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no shared channel documented, but B exposes files, stdin/stdout, browser, and MCP, while A has broad network egress and is a content-writing agent. If A’s outputs are copied into B’s workspace or MCP flow, B could treat attacker-controlled text as instructions. The pairwise bridge is inferred, not directly evidenced, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF A outputs are pasted into B’s workspace or stdin/stdout
IF B parses file or MCP content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable copy-paste handoff between agents for untrusted text
Add a provenance header to all A outputs before B reads them
Require B to treat workspace files as data, not instructions
Use a separate staging file for A outputs
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance tagging in the orchestrator

B_data_leakage.rationale: B clearly touches workspace files, audit logs, memory, and secrets, and has broad network egress. A is a content-writing agent with broad egress but no local storage surfaces shown. If A’s generated content includes sensitive material from B’s workspace, B can transmit it outward; the shared-data path is plausible in default workflows, though not directly documented.
conditions: IF B workspace files contain secrets or regulated data
IF A is given content derived from B’s workspace and then sends it over the network
mitigations: Restrict B’s workspace to non-sensitive files
Block outbound network access during review runs
Redact secrets before A processes any B-derived content
Separate credentials from shared workspace directories
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on B’s egress

C_capability_conflict.rationale: B has unrestricted write, shell, git, and network capabilities; A’s profile does not show local write surfaces, so direct conflict is asymmetric. However, B’s durable shared state and modify_git_state create a strong conflict risk if A’s outputs are materialized into the same repo or workspace. Uncertainty about A’s hidden surfaces escalates to high rather than medium.
conditions: IF A outputs are written into the same git repo or workspace B modifies
IF multiple B instances operate on the same durable namespace
mitigations: Use separate repositories per agent
Pause concurrent B instances during shared edits
Lock the workspace before git operations
Keep A outputs read-only until reviewed
requires-engineering: add optimistic-locking around shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: B has action-taking authority via shell, browser, git, and APIs, so if it consumes A’s content-writing output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions. A is not documented as verified or authoritative, and B’s sandboxing helps but does not eliminate the pathway. The interaction is plausible in default workflows, so medium fits.
conditions: IF B uses A’s output as a source of facts or instructions
IF B executes shell, browser, or git actions based on unverified A content
mitigations: Require human review before B acts on A outputs
Mark A outputs as untrusted in the handoff format
Add a verification step before commits or outbound actions
Limit B to read-only mode during A-to-B transfers
requires-engineering: implement citation and fact-check gating

E_compliance.rationale: B explicitly handles secrets, audit logs, workspace files, and webhook payloads, while A has broad network egress and no residency or retention controls shown. That creates a plausible compliance mismatch for sensitive CRM data if A receives or forwards B-originated content. A is not cited for residency because none is documented; uncertainty therefore escalates to medium.
conditions: IF B data includes regulated customer records or secrets
IF A forwards B-originated content to external services without a DPA or retention controls
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of A’s prompts and outputs
Review retention settings for B logs and workspace files
Disable outbound sharing for sensitive CRM records
Document data-flow boundaries between the agents
requires-engineering: add residency and retention policy enforcement
